entries: A plant cell, labelled - wall outside, membrane inside it, then nucleus, chloroplast and the large vacuole: the full plant kit.
slots.label: Plant cell
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: An animal cell, labelled - membrane, nucleus and mitochondrion only: no wall, no chloroplast, no large vacuole.
slots.label: Animal cell
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The membrane is the gatekeeper - food crosses in, waste crosses out, and a harmful particle is refused: the membrane chooses.
slots.label: Gatekeeper
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Two specialists: nucleus and chloroplast - the nucleus controls the cell with its instructions, the chloroplast traps light to make food.
slots.label: Specialists
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Why plants stand up straight - a full vacuole pushes the membrane against the wall so the cell is turgid; lose water and it goes flaccid.
slots.label: Turgor
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Cells team up: the organisation ladder - cell to tissue to organ to system, as in leaf cell to leaf tissue to leaf to shoot system.
slots.label: Ladder
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The smallest unit of life; every living thing is made of one or more cells, each carrying the structures it needs to stay alive.
slots.label: Cell
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A tough outer layer found in plant cells only. It gives the cell its shape and strength but is fully permeable.
slots.label: Cell wall
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The thin layer around every cell that controls what enters and leaves. It is selectively permeable.
slots.label: Cell membrane
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: Letting some substances through while keeping others out - the membrane chooses, like a gatekeeper.
slots.label: Selectively permeable
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The control centre of the cell, holding the instructions that run everything the cell does.
slots.label: Nucleus
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The plant-only structure that traps light energy to make food by photosynthesis.
slots.label: Chloroplast
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A fluid-filled space. In plant cells it is large and permanent; filled with water it pushes the cell firm.
slots.label: Vacuole
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The structure that releases energy from food, in both plant and animal cells.
slots.label: Mitochondrion
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The jelly-like substance inside the cell where most of its work happens.
slots.label: Cytoplasm
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A plant cell swollen firm because its full vacuole pushes the membrane against the wall.
slots.label: Turgid
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A group of similar cells working together at the same job, such as leaf tissue.
slots.label: Tissue
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A structure made of several tissues working together, such as a leaf or a heart.
slots.label: Organ
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A group of organs working together, such as the shoot system or the circulatory system.
slots.label: System
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
